pr_body:
Replace #28849. Thanks to @yp05327 for the looking into the problem.
Fix #28840

The old behavior of newSignatureFromCommitline is not right. The new parseSignatureFromCommitLine:

1. never fails
2. only accept one format (if there is any other, it could be easily added)

And add some tests.
pr_comments:
The output format is based on the git command, so we can control it.
And we can add other formats easily if we need.

> The output format is based on the git command, so we can control it. And we can add other formats easily if we need.

Let's only put this change in 1.22. For the backport, I will still add the legacy format support, to avoid any breaking 😄

I was unable to create a backport for 1.21. @wxiaoguang, please send one manually. :tea:

```
go run ./contrib/backport 29054
...  // fix git conflicts if any
go run ./contrib/backport --continue
```

Want to confirm:
1. It seems that you are using gogit version.
2. When creating the mirror, did you select migrate the releases?

1. Yes，I didn't know there is another gitea before your answer, now I try the no gogit version, it _works good, no error_.
2. When i use the 'import outside repo' function from top-right, I just check 'use it as a mirror' , not seen 'migrate the releases'.
3. So, _should this issue be treat as a bug_?

> now I try the no gogit version, it works good, no error.

So only gogit version has this issue. Thanks for your test.

> When i use the 'import outside repo' function from top-right, I just check 'use it as a mirror' , not seen 'migrate the releases'.

OK

> So, should this issue be treat as a bug?

Not sure. Maybe caused by some special tags in this repo, like https://github.com/go-gitea/gitea/issues/28843#issuecomment-1898213975

The reason is that the creator is empty in tag `v2.6.13-rc3`
![image](https://github.com/go-gitea/gitea/assets/18380374/0cef49ef-d981-46ef-a25c-d3076a43062a)

> The reason is that the creator is empty in tag `v2.6.13-rc3` ![image](https://private-user-images.githubusercontent.com/18380374/297918054-0cef49ef-d981-46ef-a25c-d3076a43062a.png?jwt=eyJhbGciOiJIUzI1NiIsInR5cCI6IkpXVCJ9..bfIxotXuunLdA-fbtrR2fLPFYkdeOjU5Jdd8Sb5Viic)

So we have to use a ghost here if creator is empty.

review_comments:
It seems that only `xxxxdate` can be set as other formats, but we use `creator` here which seems only using `git internal format`.
https://github.com/git/git/blob/235986be822c9f8689be2e9a0b7804d0b1b6d821/Documentation/git-for-each-ref.txt#L362-L364
All formats can be found here:
https://git-scm.com/docs/git-rev-list#Documentation/git-rev-list.txt---dateltformatgt

So maybe it is fine to ignore other formats here.
I do not see how these links are related .... the documents describe about the behaviors of some commands, but not the "internal data structure".
The only possible clue in these documents is `--date=raw`, the `raw` might mean the "raw data (time) saved in a commit object"

Why this is not:
``` text
&Signature{Name: "bad-line", Email: "name@example.com"}
```

Because it is "bad", it is not the correct format with timestamp/timezone

For a bad format, the line is save into `Name` field.
